issue_context.title: Require process privilege to access metrics_schema
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

The system database `metrics_schema` contains metrics about the cluster. To visit the load on the cluster, users need to have `PROCESS` privileges.

Besides, another 2 system tables `information_schema.metrics_summary` and `information_schema.metrics_summary_by_label` also contain metrics on the cluster.
comments:
There are some other problems:
1. Currently if the user has only `PROCESS` privilege, he still cannot see `metrics_schema` until he has `SELECT` or other privileges on `metrics_schema`. Is it reasonable? I cannot find a referential behavior in MySQL. @morgo 
2. Even if he cannot see the database, he can still select from the tables. This is a bug from the beginning.
3. Even if he cannot see the database, he can still visit `information_schema.metrics_tables`, which contains all the table definitions. Is that a problem?

```SQL
mysql> show grants for current_user;
+-----------------------------------------+
| Grants for test_user@127.0.0.1          |
+-----------------------------------------+
| GRANT PROCESS ON *.* TO 'test_user'@'%' |
+-----------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> show databases;
+--------------------+
| Database           |
+--------------------+
| INFORMATION_SCHEMA |
+--------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from metrics_schema.up limit 1;
+----------------------------+-----------------+------+-------+
| time                       | instance        | job  | value |
+----------------------------+-----------------+------+-------+
| 2021-08-25 15:40:26.860000 | 127.0.0.1:10080 | tidb |     1 |
+----------------------------+-----------------+------+-------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> show tables from metrics_schema;
ERROR 1044 (42000): Access denied for user 'test_user'@'%' to database 'metrics_schema'
mysql> select * from information_schema.metrics_tables limit 1;
+-----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------+----------+---------+
| TABLE_NAME      | PROMQL                                                                                                                                                          | LABELS        | QUANTILE | COMMENT |
+-----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------+----------+---------+
| abnormal_stores | sum(pd_cluster_status{ type=~"store_disconnected_count|store_unhealth_count|store_low_space_count|store_down_count|store_offline_count|store_tombstone_count"}) | instance,type |        0 |         |
+-----------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------+----------+---------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

> 1. Currently if the user has only `PROCESS` privilege, he still cannot see `metrics_schema` until he has `SELECT` or other privileges on `metrics_schema`. Is it reasonable? I cannot find a referential behavior in MySQL. @morgo

The behavior we can reference is a MySQL user with only usage. Here is what they can see:
```sql
mysql [localhost:8024] {uuu} ((none)) > show databases;
+--------------------+
| Database           |
+--------------------+
| information_schema |
+--------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

It might not be reasonable. We might have to instead switch our plan `PROCESS` (which is always global) to `SELECT ON metrics_schema.*`.

> 2. Even if he cannot see the database, he can still select from the tables. This is a bug from the beginning.

Agree.

> 3. Even if he cannot see the database, he can still visit `information_schema.metrics_tables`, which contains all the table definitions. Is that a problem?

Agree. Information_schema is special, in that it can show partial results based on who queries the data. It should be similar to how `information_schema.tables` filters.

> We might have to instead switch our plan `PROCESS` (which is always global) to `SELECT ON metrics_schema.*`.

Do you mean that we don't need `PROCESS` privilege to visit `metrics_schema` anymore? Only a `SELECT` (or USAGE, UPDATE, etc) privilege is enough to see the database, and `SELECT` privilege to query the tables, just like other user tables?

> `Information_schema` is special, in that it can show partial results based on who queries the data. It should be similar to how `information_schema.tables` filters.

I am afraid all the tables in `metrics_tables` are about the cluster information. So you can see all tables or you can see no tables. It's different.

After discussion, the current dicision is:
1. Need `PROCESS` or `SELECT ON metrics_schema.*`.
2. `metrics_tables` are just definitions, so it can be without checking.
3. `metrics_summary` and `metrics_summary_by_label` need `PROCESS` privilege to query.

review_comments:
If I understand this correctly, the user only requires `SelectPriv` on the database, and not the specific table? This could lead to potential privilege escalations. i.e. a user thinks it is safe to Select to one metrics table, but inadvertently grants access to all tables.

For previous `OR` behaviors (such as `DROP USER` also allowing `delete` on `mysql.user`) we have put the handing in the function directly:

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/3e8f8bbd99603bd1d49d1d99cfc5675a36202d98/executor/simple.go#L1154-L1171

I do prefer it this way.

No, it won't lead to privilege escalations. It still requires the `SELECT` privilege on the table, no the database.
But ... I found granting `SELECT` to a specific table will report an error, and so does `performance_schema`... Another bug :-(
```sql
mysql> grant select on metrics_schema.up to test_user;
ERROR 1146 (42S02): Table 'metrics_schema.up' doesn't exist
```
